set_vexpand.brief: Sets whether the widget would like any available extra vertical space.
set_vexpand.md:
Sets whether the widget would like any available extra vertical
space.

See [`Widget.set_hexpand()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#method:set_hexpand) for more detail.

set_vexpand_set.brief: Sets whether the vexpand flag will be used.
set_vexpand_set.md:
Sets whether the vexpand flag will be used.

See [`Widget.set_hexpand_set()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#method:set_hexpand_set) for more detail.

set_visible.md:
Sets the visibility state of `widget`.

Note that setting this to true doesn’t mean the widget is
actually viewable, see [`Widget.get_visible()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#method:get_visible).

should_layout.brief: Returns whether the widget should contribute to the measuring and allocation of its parent.
should_layout.md:
Returns whether the widget should contribute to
the measuring and allocation of its parent.

This is false for invisible children, but also
for children that have their own surface, such
as [`Popover`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Popover) instances.

show.brief: Flags a widget to be displayed.
show.md:
Flags a widget to be displayed.

Any widget that isn’t shown will not appear on the screen.

Remember that you have to show the containers containing a widget,
in addition to the widget itself, before it will appear onscreen.

When a toplevel widget is shown, it is immediately realized and
mapped; other shown widgets are realized and mapped when their
toplevel widget is realized and mapped.

size_allocate.brief: Allocates widget with a transformation that translates the origin to the position in `allocation`.
size_allocate.md:
Allocates widget with a transformation that translates
the origin to the position in `allocation`.

This is a simple form of [`Widget.allocate()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#method:allocate).

snapshot_child.brief: Snapshots a child of the widget.
snapshot_child.md:
Snapshots a child of the widget.

When a widget receives a call to the snapshot function,
it must send synthetic [`Widget.snapshot()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#vfunc:snapshot) calls
to all children. This function provides a convenient way
of doing this. A widget, when it receives a call to its
[`Widget.snapshot()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#vfunc:snapshot) function, calls
gtk_widget_snapshot_child() once for each child, passing in
the `snapshot` the widget received.

This function takes care of translating the origin of `snapshot`,
and deciding whether the child needs to be snapshot.

It does nothing for children that implement `GtkNative`.

translate_coordinates.brief: Translates coordinates relative to `src_widget`’s allocation to coordinates relative to `dest_widget`’s allocations.
translate_coordinates.md:
Translates coordinates relative to `src_widget`’s allocation
to coordinates relative to `dest_widget`’s allocations.

In order to perform this operation, both widget must share
a common ancestor. If that is not the case, `dest_x` and `dest_y`
are set to 0 and false is returned.

trigger_tooltip_query.brief: Triggers a tooltip query on the display of the widget.
trigger_tooltip_query.md: Triggers a tooltip query on the display of the widget.

unmap.brief: Causes a widget to be unmapped if it’s currently mapped.
unmap.md:
Causes a widget to be unmapped if it’s currently mapped.

This function is only for use in widget implementations.

unparent.md:
Removes `widget` from its parent.

This function is only for use in widget implementations,
typically in dispose.

unrealize.brief: Causes a widget to be unrealized.
unrealize.md:
Causes a widget to be unrealized.

This frees all GDK resources associated with the widget.

This function is only useful in widget implementations.

unset_state_flags.brief: Turns off flag values for the current widget state.
unset_state_flags.md:
Turns off flag values for the current widget state.

See [`Widget.set_state_flags()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#method:set_state_flags).

This function is for use in widget implementations.

can-focus.brief: Whether the widget or any of its descendents can accept the input focus.
can-focus.md:
Whether the widget or any of its descendents can accept
the input focus.

This property is meant to be set by widget implementations,
typically in their instance init function.

can-target.brief: Whether the widget can receive pointer events.
can-target.md: Whether the widget can receive pointer events.

css-classes.brief: A list of css classes applied to this widget.
css-classes.md: A list of css classes applied to this widget.

css-name.brief: The name of this widget in the CSS tree.
css-name.md:
The name of this widget in the CSS tree.

This property is meant to be set by widget implementations,
typically in their instance init function.

focus-on-click.brief: Whether the widget should grab focus when it is clicked with the mouse.
focus-on-click.md:
Whether the widget should grab focus when it is clicked with the mouse.

This property is only relevant for widgets that can take focus.

focusable.brief: Whether this widget itself will accept the input focus.
focusable.md: Whether this widget itself will accept the input focus.

halign.brief: How to distribute horizontal space if widget gets extra space.
halign.md: How to distribute horizontal space if widget gets extra space.

has-default.brief: Whether the widget is the default widget.
has-default.md: Whether the widget is the default widget.

has-focus.brief: Whether the widget has the input focus.
has-focus.md: Whether the widget has the input focus.

has-tooltip.brief: Enables or disables the emission of the [`Widget::query-tooltip`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#event:query-tooltip) signal on `widget`.
has-tooltip.md:
Enables or disables the emission of the [`Widget::query-tooltip`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#event:query-tooltip)
signal on `widget`.

A true value indicates that `widget` can have a tooltip, in this case
the widget will be queried using [`Widget::query-tooltip`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#event:query-tooltip) to
determine whether it will provide a tooltip or not.

height-request.brief: Overrides for height request of the widget.
height-request.md:
Overrides for height request of the widget.

If this is -1, the natural request will be used.

layout-manager.brief: The [`LayoutManager`](xref:gtk:Gtk.LayoutManager) instance to use to compute the preferred size of the widget, and allocate its children.
layout-manager.md:
The [`LayoutManager`](xref:gtk:Gtk.LayoutManager) instance to use to compute
the preferred size of the widget, and allocate its children.

This property is meant to be set by widget implementations,
typically in their instance init function.

limit-events.brief: Makes this widget act like a modal dialog, with respect to event delivery.
limit-events.md:
Makes this widget act like a modal dialog, with respect to
event delivery.

Global event controllers will not handle events with targets
inside the widget, unless they are set up to ignore propagation
limits. See [`EventController.set_propagation_limit()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.EventController#method:set_propagation_limit).

margin-bottom.brief: Margin on bottom side of widget.
margin-bottom.md:
Margin on bottom side of widget.

This property adds margin outside of the widget's normal size
request, the margin will be added in addition to the size from
[`Widget.set_size_request()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#method:set_size_request) for example.

margin-end.brief: Margin on end of widget, horizontally.
margin-end.md:
Margin on end of widget, horizontally.

This property supports left-to-right and right-to-left text
directions.

This property adds margin outside of the widget's normal size
request, the margin will be added in addition to the size from
[`Widget.set_size_request()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#method:set_size_request) for example.

margin-start.brief: Margin on start of widget, horizontally.
margin-start.md:
Margin on start of widget, horizontally.

This property supports left-to-right and right-to-left text
directions.

This property adds margin outside of the widget's normal size
request, the margin will be added in addition to the size from
[`Widget.set_size_request()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#method:set_size_request) for example.

margin-top.brief: Margin on top side of widget.
margin-top.md:
Margin on top side of widget.

This property adds margin outside of the widget's normal size
request, the margin will be added in addition to the size from
[`Widget.set_size_request()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#method:set_size_request) for example.

opacity.brief: The requested opacity of the widget.
opacity.md: The requested opacity of the widget.

overflow.brief: How content outside the widget's content area is treated.
overflow.md:
How content outside the widget's content area is treated.

This property is meant to be set by widget implementations,
typically in their instance init function.

parent.brief: The parent widget of this widget.
parent.md: The parent widget of this widget.

receives-default.brief: Whether the widget will receive the default action when it is focused.
receives-default.md: Whether the widget will receive the default action when it is focused.

root.brief: The `GtkRoot` widget of the widget tree containing this widget.
root.md:
The `GtkRoot` widget of the widget tree containing this widget.

This will be `NULL` if the widget is not contained in a root widget.

scale-factor.brief: The scale factor of the widget.
scale-factor.md: The scale factor of the widget.

sensitive.brief: Whether the widget responds to input.
sensitive.md: Whether the widget responds to input.

tooltip-markup.brief: Sets the text of tooltip to be the given string, which is marked up with Pango markup.
tooltip-markup.md:
Sets the text of tooltip to be the given string, which is marked up
with Pango markup.

Also see [`Tooltip.set_markup()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Tooltip#method:set_markup).

This is a convenience property which will take care of getting the
tooltip shown if the given string is not `NULL`:
[`Widget:has-tooltip`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#property:has-tooltip) will automatically be set to true
and there will be taken care of [`Widget::query-tooltip`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#event:query-tooltip) in
the default signal handler.

Note that if both [`Widget:tooltip-text`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#property:tooltip-text) and
[`Widget:tooltip-markup`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#property:tooltip-markup) are set, the last one wins.

tooltip-text.brief: Sets the text of tooltip to be the given string.
tooltip-text.md:
Sets the text of tooltip to be the given string.

Also see [`Tooltip.set_text()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Tooltip#method:set_text).

This is a convenience property which will take care of getting the
tooltip shown if the given string is not `NULL`:
[`Widget:has-tooltip`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#property:has-tooltip) will automatically be set to true
and there will be taken care of [`Widget::query-tooltip`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#event:query-tooltip) in
the default signal handler.

Note that if both [`Widget:tooltip-text`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#property:tooltip-text) and
[`Widget:tooltip-markup`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#property:tooltip-markup) are set, the last one wins.

valign.brief: How to distribute vertical space if widget gets extra space.
valign.md: How to distribute vertical space if widget gets extra space.

width-request.brief: Overrides for width request of the widget.
width-request.md:
Overrides for width request of the widget.

If this is -1, the natural request will be used.

destroy.brief: Signals that all holders of a reference to the widget should release the reference that they hold.
destroy.md:
Signals that all holders of a reference to the widget should release
the reference that they hold.

May result in finalization of the widget if all references are released.

This signal is not suitable for saving widget state.

direction-changed.brief: Emitted when the text direction of a widget changes.
direction-changed.md: Emitted when the text direction of a widget changes.

keynav-failed.md:
Emitted if keyboard navigation fails.

See [`Widget.keynav_failed()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#method:keynav_failed) for details.

map.brief: Emitted when `widget` is going to be mapped.
map.md:
Emitted when `widget` is going to be mapped.

A widget is mapped when the widget is visible (which is controlled with
[`Widget:visible`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#property:visible)) and all its parents up to the toplevel widget
are also visible.

The `::map` signal can be used to determine whether a widget will be drawn,
for instance it can resume an animation that was stopped during the
emission of [`Widget::unmap`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#event:unmap).

mnemonic-activate.brief: Emitted when a widget is activated via a mnemonic.
mnemonic-activate.md:
Emitted when a widget is activated via a mnemonic.

The default handler for this signal activates `widget` if `group_cycling`
is false, or just makes `widget` grab focus if `group_cycling` is true.

move-focus.brief: Emitted when the focus is moved.
move-focus.md:
Emitted when the focus is moved.

The `::move-focus` signal is a [keybinding signal](class.SignalAction.html).

The default bindings for this signal are <kbd>Tab</kbd> to move forward,
and <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Tab</kbd> to move backward.

query-tooltip.brief: Emitted when the widget’s tooltip is about to be shown.
query-tooltip.md:
Emitted when the widget’s tooltip is about to be shown.

This happens when the [`Widget:has-tooltip`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#property:has-tooltip) property
is true and the hover timeout has expired with the cursor hovering
above `widget`; or emitted when `widget` got focus in keyboard mode.

Using the given coordinates, the signal handler should determine
whether a tooltip should be shown for `widget`. If this is the case
true should be returned, false otherwise. Note that if `keyboard_mode`
is true, the values of `x` and `y` are undefined and should not be used.

The signal handler is free to manipulate `tooltip` with the therefore
destined function calls.

realize.brief: Emitted when `widget` is associated with a `GdkSurface`.
realize.md:
Emitted when `widget` is associated with a `GdkSurface`.

This means that [`Widget.realize()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#method:realize) has been called
or the widget has been mapped (that is, it is going to be drawn).

state-flags-changed.brief: Emitted when the widget state changes.
state-flags-changed.md:
Emitted when the widget state changes.

See [`Widget.get_state_flags()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#method:get_state_flags).

unmap.brief: Emitted when `widget` is going to be unmapped.
unmap.md:
Emitted when `widget` is going to be unmapped.

A widget is unmapped when either it or any of its parents up to the
toplevel widget have been set as hidden.

As `::unmap` indicates that a widget will not be shown any longer,
it can be used to, for example, stop an animation on the widget.

unrealize.brief: Emitted when the `GdkSurface` associated with `widget` is destroyed.
unrealize.md:
Emitted when the `GdkSurface` associated with `widget` is destroyed.

This means that [`Widget.unrealize()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#method:unrealize) has been called
or the widget has been unmapped (that is, it is going to be hidden).

compute_expand.brief: Computes whether a container should give this widget extra space when possible.
compute_expand.md:
Computes whether a container should give this
  widget extra space when possible.

contains.brief: Tests if a given point is contained in the widget.
contains.md:
Tests if a given point is contained in the widget.

The coordinates for (x, y) must be in widget coordinates, so
(0, 0) is assumed to be the top left of `widget`'s content area.

css_changed.brief: Vfunc called when the CSS used by widget was changed.
css_changed.md:
Vfunc called when the CSS used by widget was changed. Widgets
  should then discard their caches that depend on CSS and queue resizes or
  redraws accordingly. The default implementation will take care of this for
  all the default CSS properties, so implementations must chain up.

direction_changed.brief: Signal emitted when the text direction of a widget changes.
direction_changed.md:
Signal emitted when the text direction of a
  widget changes.

get_request_mode.brief: Gets whether the widget prefers a height-for-width layout or a width-for-height layout.
get_request_mode.md:
Gets whether the widget prefers a height-for-width layout
or a width-for-height layout.

Single-child widgets generally propagate the preference of
their child, more complex widgets need to request something
either in context of their children or in context of their
allocation capabilities.

grab_focus.brief: Causes `widget` to have the keyboard focus for the window that it belongs to.
grab_focus.md:
Causes `widget` to have the keyboard focus for the window
that it belongs to.

If `widget` is not focusable, or its [`Widget.grab_focus()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#vfunc:grab_focus)
implementation cannot transfer the focus to a descendant of `widget`
that is focusable, it will not take focus and false will be returned.

Calling [`Widget.grab_focus()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#method:grab_focus) on an already focused widget
is allowed, should not have an effect, and return true.

hide.md:
Reverses the effects of [method.Gtk.Widget.show].

This is causing the widget to be hidden (invisible to the user).

keynav_failed.brief: Emits the [`Widget::keynav-failed`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#event:keynav-failed) signal on the widget.
keynav_failed.md:
Emits the [`Widget::keynav-failed`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#event:keynav-failed) signal on the widget.

This function should be called whenever keyboard navigation
within a single widget hits a boundary.

The return value of this function should be interpreted
in a way similar to the return value of
[`Widget.child_focus()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#method:child_focus). When true is returned,
stay in the widget, the failed keyboard navigation is ok
and/or there is nowhere we can/should move the focus to.
When false is returned, the caller should continue with
keyboard navigation outside the widget, e.g. by calling
[`Widget.child_focus()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#method:child_focus) on the widget’s toplevel.

The default [`Widget::keynav-failed`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#event:keynav-failed) handler returns
false for [`DirectionType.tab-forward`](xref:gtk:Gtk.DirectionType#value:tab-forward) and
[`DirectionType.tab-backward`](xref:gtk:Gtk.DirectionType#value:tab-backward). For the other values
of [`DirectionType`](xref:gtk:Gtk.DirectionType) it returns true.

Whenever the default handler returns true, it also calls
[`Widget.error_bell()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#method:error_bell) to notify the user of the
failed keyboard navigation.

A use case for providing an own implementation of `::keynav-failed`
(either by connecting to it or by overriding it) would be a row of
[`Entry`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Entry) widgets where the user should be able to navigate
the entire row with the cursor keys, as e.g. known from user
interfaces that require entering license keys.

map.brief: Causes a widget to be mapped if it isn’t already.
map.md:
Causes a widget to be mapped if it isn’t already.

This function is only for use in widget implementations.

measure.brief: Measures `widget` in the orientation `orientation` and for the given `for_size`.
measure.md:
Measures `widget` in the orientation `orientation` and for the given `for_size`.

As an example, if `orientation` is %GTK_ORIENTATION_HORIZONTAL and `for_size`
is 300, this functions will compute the minimum and natural width of `widget`
if it is allocated at a height of 300 pixels.

See [GtkWidget’s geometry management section](class.Widget.html#height-for-width-geometry-management) for
a more details on implementing `GtkWidgetClass.measure()`.

move_focus.brief: Signal emitted when a change of focus is requested
move_focus.md: Signal emitted when a change of focus is requested

query_tooltip.brief: Signal emitted when “has-tooltip” is `TRUE` and the hover timeout has expired with the cursor hovering “above” widget; or emitted when widget got focus in keyboard mode.
query_tooltip.md:
Signal emitted when “has-tooltip” is `TRUE` and the
  hover timeout has expired with the cursor hovering “above”
  widget; or emitted when widget got focus in keyboard mode.

realize.brief: Creates the GDK resources associated with a widget.
realize.md:
Creates the GDK resources associated with a widget.

Normally realization happens implicitly; if you show a widget
and all its parent containers, then the widget will be realized
and mapped automatically.

Realizing a widget requires all the widget’s parent widgets to be
realized; calling this function realizes the widget’s parents
in addition to `widget` itself. If a widget is not yet inside a
toplevel window when you realize it, bad things will happen.

This function is primarily used in widget implementations, and
isn’t very useful otherwise. Many times when you think you might
need it, a better approach is to connect to a signal that will be
called after the widget is realized automatically, such as
[`Widget::realize`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#event:realize).

root.brief: Called when the widget gets added to a `GtkRoot` widget.
root.md:
Called when the widget gets added to a `GtkRoot` widget. Must
  chain up

set_focus_child.brief: Set the focus child of the widget.
set_focus_child.md:
Set the focus child of the widget.

This function is only suitable for widget implementations.
If you want a certain widget to get the input focus, call
[`Widget.grab_focus()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Widget#method:grab_focus) on it.

show.brief: Flags a widget to be displayed.
show.md:
Flags a widget to be displayed.

Any widget that isn’t shown will not appear on the screen.

Remember that you have to show the containers containing a widget,
in addition to the widget itself, before it will appear onscreen.

When a toplevel widget is shown, it is immediately realized and
mapped; other shown widgets are realized and mapped when their
toplevel widget is realized and mapped.

size_allocate.brief: Called to set the allocation, if the widget does not have a layout manager.
size_allocate.md:
Called to set the allocation, if the widget does
  not have a layout manager.

snapshot.brief: Vfunc called when a new snapshot of the widget has to be taken.
snapshot.md: Vfunc called when a new snapshot of the widget has to be taken.

state_flags_changed.brief: Signal emitted when the widget state changes, see gtk_widget_get_state_flags().
state_flags_changed.md:
Signal emitted when the widget state changes,
  see gtk_widget_get_state_flags().

system_setting_changed.brief: Emitted when a system setting was changed.
system_setting_changed.md: Emitted when a system setting was changed. Must chain up.

unmap.brief: Causes a widget to be unmapped if it’s currently mapped.
unmap.md:
Causes a widget to be unmapped if it’s currently mapped.

This function is only for use in widget implementations.

unrealize.brief: Causes a widget to be unrealized.
unrealize.md:
Causes a widget to be unrealized.

This frees all GDK resources associated with the widget.

This function is only useful in widget implementations.

unroot.brief: Called when the widget is about to be removed from its `GtkRoot` widget.
unroot.md:
Called when the widget is about to be removed from its
  `GtkRoot` widget. Must chain up
